authoritative_sources.name: FAO Global Forest Resources Assessment (FRA 2020 / 2025)
authoritative_sources.organization: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)
indicators: Share of Land Covered by Forest (%)
authoritative_sources.methodology: National reporting, remote sensing surveys, peer-reviewed expert validation across 5-year intervals with annual trend harmonizations.
authoritative_sources.type: Directly Measured & Officially Reported Ground/Satellite Observation

authoritative_sources.name: Global Forest Watch / Curtis et al. (Science 2018)
authoritative_sources.organization: World Resources Institute (WRI) & University of Maryland
indicators: Tree Cover Loss by Dominant Driver (Permanent agriculture, Logging, Shifting cultivation, Wildfire, Settlements/infrastructure, Mining)
authoritative_sources.methodology: Machine-learning classification of Landsat satellite time series at 30-meter resolution identifying direct proximate physical drivers.

authoritative_sources.name: Agricultural Commodity Drivers of Deforestation (Pendrill et al. 2022)
authoritative_sources.organization: Chalmers University of Technology, Stockholm Environment Institute, FAO
authoritative_sources.publication: Pendrill et al., Environmental Research Letters (2022)
indicators: Deforestation attributable to Beef, Soy, Palm Oil, Wood Fiber, Cocoa, Coffee, Cereals, Roots & Tubers
authoritative_sources.methodology: Coupling spatial land-use change mapping with FAOSTAT agricultural production data and physical supply-chain trade models.
authoritative_sources.type: Inferred Economic Attribution from Measured Spatial Clearing

authoritative_sources.name: Global Carbon Budget (Friedlingstein et al. 2023 / 2024)
indicators: Annual CO2 Emissions from Land-Use Change (tonnes CO2/yr)
authoritative_sources.methodology: Ensemble of bookkeeping models (BLUE, OSCAR, H&N) driven by FAO forest area change data and deforestation dynamics.
authoritative_sources.type: Biogeochemical Bookkeeping Modeling based on Measured Land-Use Changes

authoritative_sources.name: IUCN Red List Index
authoritative_sources.organization: International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) & BirdLife International
indicators: Red List Index (0.0 = all species extinct, 1.0 = all species least concern)
authoritative_sources.methodology: Aggregate measure of extinction risk changes over time for birds, mammals, amphibians, corals, and cycads.

distinction_notice.measured_causes: Curtis et al. drivers (permanent agriculture, shifting cultivation, logging, wildfire, settlements/infrastructure, mining) represent directly observed physical land-cover disturbances classified from 30m satellite imagery.
distinction_notice.inferred_causes: Pendrill et al. commodity drivers (beef cattle ranching, soy, palm oil, forestry, cocoa/coffee) are inferred through econometric allocation models linking observed spatial clearance to national crop/livestock production statistics and international trade flows.
distinction_notice.data_availability_notes: Official FAO national forest inventory reports are compiled periodically (1990, 2000, 2010, 2015, 2020) with annual harmonized updates through 2025. Direct driver data spans 2001–2024; commodity attribution spans 2001–2023. For missing observations, 'Data Not Available' is shown.
